desc:
Shopify app integrations and API connections link your app to the tools merchants already use, such as Klaviyo, Google Analytics, shipping services or your own backend. Ecom Swift LLC builds each connection with safe key storage, retries and clear admin messages.

## What is a Shopify app integration?

A Shopify app integration is a connection between your app and an outside service, so data moves between them without manual work. A merchant connects their email platform, and customer segments sync. An order is created, and a shipping label request goes out. A product changes, and your backend hears about it. Each connection has a direction, a trigger, a data format and a plan for what happens when something fails.

## Why integrations are where apps break

Integrations depend on systems you do not control. Services change their endpoints, tokens expire, rate limits tighten and responses arrive late or not at all. An integration that works in a demo can fail quietly in production, leaving merchants with missing orders or stale stock, and no message explaining why.

Good integration work assumes failure. It stores credentials safely, retries calls that fail for temporary reasons, records what happened and tells the merchant in plain words when action is needed.

## How connections change the merchant's day

Merchants judge an app by how much manual work it removes. An integration that copies orders into an accounting tool saves an evening of spreadsheet entry. A sync that pushes customers to an email platform keeps campaigns current without exports. When these connections are reliable, the app becomes part of how the store runs, and merchants are less likely to remove it.

Visibility matters as much as automation. A log page that shows what synced and what failed turns support questions into self-service answers.

## What a dependable integration includes

- Authentication through OAuth where the service offers it, or encrypted storage of API keys where it does not.
- Field mapping, so merchants can match their data to the other tool's fields.
- Webhook subscriptions on the Shopify side, managed so they do not duplicate.
- A retry queue with sensible waiting between attempts.
- Handling of the other service's rate limits.
- Two-way sync for products or orders, where the use case needs it.
- On and off settings, so merchants control what is shared.
- An integration log with clear success and error entries.
- Sandbox testing and a written guide for your team.

## How we build them

We start with a data map: what moves, in which direction, what triggers it and what counts as a conflict. We then connect using the other service's sandbox or test account, build the sync and test the failure cases deliberately, such as expired tokens, timeouts and malformed responses.

Basic connects one tool and syncs one type of data. Standard connects up to three tools with merchant settings, a retry queue and a log page. Premium covers a larger set with field mapping, webhook management, rate limit handling and an integration guide. Any fees charged by the connected services are paid by you directly to them.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Decide which system is the source of truth for each field.
- Give us sandbox or test accounts for every service.
- Ask merchants for the minimum permissions on the other tool.
- Show merchants a plain message when a sync fails.

**Avoid:**
- Storing API keys in plain text or in the browser.
- Syncing everything when only a few fields are needed.
- Assuming the other service is always online.
- Letting two systems edit the same field with no rule for conflicts.

## Who this service is for

App owners whose merchants keep asking for one more connection. Businesses that need their Shopify data to reach a warehouse, accounting tool or internal system. Developers who want a second pair of hands on a service with a tricky API.

## What we need from you

A list of the tools to connect, test or sandbox access for each, and documentation links if the service is unusual. We also need access to your repository and Partner account as a collaborator or developer user. We never ask for passwords, and live credentials are entered by you into the app's own settings.
